P42 lane S (D-CSUBSET-BITINT-ZERO-LITERAL-EATEN-BY-THE-OCTAL-PREFIX): the BARE ZERO bit-precise literal. C spells the octal prefix `0`, so for the literal `0` the longest-declared-prefix scan consumed the ONLY digit and left an EMPTY body — and the two sibling decoders of that one grammar disagreed about what an empty body means. `decodeInteger` has no 'no digits' verdict and returned 0; `decodeBigInteger` (the wb/uwb path) returned nullopt, which its caller renders as S_IntegerLiteralTooLarge. ✔MEASURED with the shipped CLI before the fix, rc=1 in EVERY context: `error[S0012]` on `0wb`, `0uwb`, `0WB`, `0Uwb`, `0wbu`, on the file-scope initializer, on the cast, on the arithmetic operand, on the array dimension, on the case label, and `error[S000F]` on the enumerator.
★★ ONLY THE BARE DECIMAL SPELLING FAILED, which is why this is a corpus example and not only a unit pin: `00wb`, `0x0wb`, `0b0wb` and `010wb` all compiled and RAN correctly beforehand, so every neighbouring rung of the ladder looked healthy. The refutation matters — the first hypothesis handed to the lane that found this was the width ladder / `integerLiteralTyping`, and it was wrong in both halves; the ladder represents zero fine, and the declared `{"prefix":"0","radix":8}` entry IS consumed (`010wb` runs as 8).
★ REFERENCE GROUND TRUTH, each probed SEPARATELY: clang 18.1.3 `-std=c23` compiles and runs every construct in this file (`0wb` → 0, `010wb` → 8, and the same under `-std=c2x`). gcc 13.3.0 has NO `_BitInt` at all — `-std=c2x` reports `implicit declaration of function '_BitInt'` and `invalid suffix "wb" on integer constant` — so clang alone is the witness, which is sufficient under `DSS = (gcc ∪ clang ∪ MSVC) ∪ ISO C`: the rule is the DISJUNCTION, and a reference's failure is never evidence against DSS.
★★ EXIT 42 IS LOAD-BEARING AND SEPARATES THE TWO FAILURE MODES, which is the point of the arithmetic rather than decoration. Revert the decoder and the program does not COMPILE (S0012). 'Fix' it instead with the tempting shortcut — return zero whenever the digit body is empty — and `010wb` still decodes as 8 but the shortcut cannot distinguish a standalone digit-valued prefix from a prefix whose digits were discarded; the shipped rule keeps the prefix as the body ONLY when removing it would empty the body, and the `oct` term is what witnesses that the marker reading still applies when a body follows. A `volatile` seed keeps every value runtime-dependent so the release optimizer cannot fold the file to a constant and pass vacuously.
★ WHAT THE FIX WAS, stated because the tier matters: NOT the semantic tier. Patching `typeLiteralIfAny` would have copied the literal normalization a THIRD time and left `cst_const_eval.cpp` and `cst_to_hir.cpp` — the array-dimension, enumerator, case-label and file-scope-initializer paths in this file — still broken, masked only because the semantic tier reports first. The suffix strip, separator strip and prefix resolution were written out THREE times in `number_decode.hpp`; they are now ONE `normalizeIntegerLiteral`, and the digit map is one `digitValue`. Both previously-masked callers were fixed with NO edit to their files, which this example verifies by execution.
